Whether you're moving across the country or buying a car online, it's not always practical to get behind the wheel and drive it home yourself. Instead, you can hire a reliable auto transport company who specializes in this service.  Car shipping is popular, and convenient. It can also range from economical to pricey. According to Consumer Affairs, vehicle transport costs range from $0.53 to $2.30 per mile. 

Finding the right company for the job can take some homework. Car shipping companies called brokers specialize in helping people connect with reputable car haulers. Other car shipper companies are carriers who own the rigs themselves. The internet is full of car shipping horror stories, however, so knowing who to trust can be challenging. 

We sought to answer this question by rigorously researching car companies. We read scores of customer reviews, reached out to the companies themselves for estimates and input, and analyzed industry trends. We also developed a car shipper grading system you can use to determine the best auto transport company for your specific needs. 

We feel confident recommending AmeriFreight Auto Transport as the overall best car shipping company, but if you're looking for the most affordable quotes or a broker that specializes in custom requests, keep reading to find your match. 

Learn more about how sponsored placements work at Move.org.

What we look for in a good car shipping company

Price transparency

Final price is guaranteed or close to the original quote, with no hidden fees 

Insurance coverage

Automatic coverage beyond the legal minimums, plus optional gap coverage

Reliability

A reputation for on-time delivery and excellent customer service

Carrier quality

A thorough carrier vetting process and high customer satisfaction

Montway Auto Transport has been around for nearly two decades, and that experience shows in their ability to easily accommodate tricky transports. Whether your car has low clearance or a lift kit, is at an auction house or a port — or doesn't even run — Montway can find a qualified carrier. It's also one of the only car shipping companies that will transport vehicles to and from the U.S. territories of Puerto Rico and Guam.

The good and the bad
5-star review: "I had my car transported from the west coast to the east coast and it arrived one day early in perfect condition. The only slight hitch was, for some unknown reason, the car pick up was 10 blocks from my home. Other than that, the delivery was excellent." —Thomas S. via BBB, 10/18/2025

1-star review: "The one star review is for the driver they used. He was rude to both the seller of my car in California as well as myself. Poor communication. He also made me walk 15 min. in the rain to meet him with my car; he wouldn’t come to my street to drop the car because he said he was not “pizza delivery” even though my street is more than wide enough to fit his truck." —Andrew L. via Trustpilot, 8/23/2025
Pro tip: Door-to-door sometimes means street-to-street

Sometimes door-to-door pickup and delivery isn't feasible if roads are narrow or regulations forbid heavy vehicles and semis. You might need to meet in a more suitable pick-up location, like a parking lot or roomy street. Carriers may communicate these requirements in advance, but sometimes they have to make last-minute decisions based on real-time road conditions.

This company offers door-to-door shipping. You may wish to consider a larger brokerage like AmeriFreight or Montway if you want to ship a car to or from a storage facility, auction, or shipping terminal.

The marketplace approach seems to work well for most people, as uShip has an average customer rating of 4.5 out of 5 stars from more than 13,000 reviews. You need to watch out for low-quality carriers, so look for ones with a strong reputation.

As part of its "Ship With Confidence" guarantee, uShip will reimburse you up to $500 if you prepaid for car shipping and the carrier never showed up. You can also get up to $500 if your vehicle is stolen or damaged and insurance doesn't cover the loss. Paying for an optional uShip Protection Plan gives you additional protection.

How do car shipping companies work?

Car shipping companies can be divided into two categories: carriers and brokers.

  • Carriers are also called haulers or drivers. They're the ones who actually pick up and deliver your vehicle. 
  • Brokers are companies that specialize in matching carriers with customers. They don't employ carriers directly but maintain a network of dependable drivers they like to work with. 

The car shipping companies on our list are brokers. Instead of vetting individual drivers and small transport companies ourselves, we found the best companies that already have a network of high-quality drivers.

Here's how the process typically works.

1. Talk to a representative. When you work with a car shipping broker, a representative will ask for basic details like the make and model of the car and the pick-up and drop-off locations. They'll also note whether you have specific requests, like an enclosed transport trailer or top-load preference. You may be able to fill out an online form instead, but it's best to talk to someone if you have a unique or modified vehicle or any special requests.

2. Wait for bids. Your transport details are posted to the company's private job board. Interested carriers will bid on your job. Each carrier bids a slightly lower price than the previous carrier in an effort to win the job. In most cases, the lowest bid wins. Sometimes you get to hand-select the carrier from the list of bidders.

3. Select carrier and pay deposit. Once your carrier has been selected, you'll typically pay some or all of the cost with a debit or credit card. If you make a partial payment, the remainder of the cost is paid in cash to the carrier upon delivery. Some brokers offer a discount for these cash transactions. 

4. Schedule pick up. Once you've paid, your pick-up window will be confirmed. Usually you'll hear directly from the carrier when they're en route to your pick-up location. You may be notified only a few hours in advance. You need to be present during pick-up in order to sign the bill of lading, a document that itemizes any pre-existing damage on the vehicle. 

5. Prepare for delivery. You'll hear from the carrier again when they're headed to your delivery location. Some brokers facilitate frequent location updates so you know where your vehicle is throughout the shipping process. Others are relatively quiet. 

6. Sign off and pay remainder. When your car is unloaded from the trailer, you'll need to inspect it for damage and update the bill of lading. You'll pay the delivery driver the cash payment at this point, if applicable, and receive the keys. 

Continue reading: How do I get a car shipping quote?

Pro tip: Empty your vehicle before pickup

Most brokers and carriers allow only 100 pounds' worth of personal items in the car, if any at all. Some have very specific rules about how those items can be packaged and where they can be located.

For a smooth pickup experience, learn how to prep your car for transport.

How much does it cost to ship a car?

The cost to ship a car depends on several factors, including total distance, proximity to major highways, time of year, type of transport carrier, and vehicle size, modifications, and operability.  

We calculate the average cost to ship a running sedan is about $1.89 per mile on an open transport carrier and $2.82 per mile on an enclosed transport carrier. This comes to about $914 (open) to $1,342 (closed) for the average trip.

Shipping a larger vehicle, like a pickup truck, can increase the price by nearly 40%. Vehicles that don't brake, steer, or roll tend to require special trailers, which cost an extra $215 on average.

Insider tips for saving money on car shipping

Car shipping can be expensive. Here's how to keep costs to a minimum. 

  • Book in advance. Rush jobs tend to cost more because carriers have less time to bid. You'll get fewer bids overall and the price won't go as low as possible.
  • Choose an open carrier. They're more common and therefore more affordable than enclosed trailers. 
  • Drive the car to a more convenient pick-up point. Carriers may be more willing to bid on your job if the pick-up point is on their existing route. You could get a better deal by bringing the car to the closest major city or a town near the freeway. 
  • Pay the remainder of your bill in cash. Some car shipping companies offer discounts of about $50 if you pay the driver cash at delivery.
  • Ask about discounts. Car shipping companies sometimes offer discounts for seniors, military members, law enforcement officers, and more. 
  • Request price matching. Get quotes from multiple car shipping companies. See if your favorite option will price match the most affordable one.

Continue reading: How do I get the best deals and discounts on car shipping?

"Buyers have strong negotiating power. The sheer number of vehicle shipping service providers in the U.S. enables consumers to switch suppliers with ease, forcing companies to compete on several fronts."

IbisWorld — Industry Research Leader

How do I choose a reliable car shipping company?

A car shipping company should fit into your budget and schedule, provide excellent communication, and take good care of your vehicle.

Consider the following when choosing a car shipping company: 

  • Reasonable prices. Avoid overpaying by taking the extra time to compare multiple quotes. Beware of estimates that seem too good to be true, though. 
  • Guaranteed quotes. We’ve often seen car shipping prices go up about 25% between the initial estimate and the final price, so consider it a green flag if a company guarantees even a portion of your shipping quote.
  • Years of experience. Longevity is generally a huge trust signal in the car shipping industry. We recommend looking for a company that’s been around for a while.
  • Extra insurance coverage. Accidents are rare — but in logistics, anything can happen. The best companies will offer you more than a bare-bones insurance policy. 
  • Reputation. Read recent customer reviews to evaluate the car shipping company's reliability. If a significant number of reviewers say their vehicle was picked up or delivered late, consider another company. 
  • Communication. If you're having a hard time getting a straight answer about a quote or can't get someone on the phone to ask an insurance question, don't expect things to change once you're a paying customer. A good car shipping company will prioritize communication. 
  • Proper licenses: You can tell an auto transport company is legit by checking for  a Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) license. 
I shipped a car from New York City to Los Angeles
"I valued clear pricing, customer reviews and communication, when picking a shipping company. So I sought a provider that gave me good real-time tracking and responsive support and had a record of on-time delivery. An issue for this cross-country move, especially, was reliability over speed.

I used Montway Auto Transport and it went well. The pickup went smoothly, the driver maintained communication throughout the journey, and the car arrived in fantastic condition. If I had to do it again, I would book earlier to avoid limited availability during peak weeks."
—Amra Beganovich, Montway customer via personal interview, 4/18/2025

Consider the services you need

Door-to-door shipping on an open transport carrier is the most common offering in the car shipping world. But if you're interested in these services, you may have fewer car shipping companies to choose from:

  • Terminal shipping: If you can't be present for pick-up and delivery, consider dropping off your car at a secure facility called a terminal. The driver will pick it up there. AmeriFreight, Montway, and SGT offer terminal shipping.
  • Same-day pickup: Urgent pickups are often needed when another transport company drops the ball. AmeriFreight, Sherpa Auto Transport, and Ship a Car Direct are willing to help you find a carrier for same-day pickup. 
  • Guaranteed delivery date: This is extremely rare because carriers' schedules are beholden to traffic, weather, mechanical breakdowns, and rules and regulations about how many hours they can spend on the road in a given day. We have yet to find a reputable car shipping company that offers this guarantee.
  • Vehicle storage: Some companies are willing to find a driver who can drop your car off at a storage facility. Others consider this too much of a hassle. 
  • GPS tracking: Some car carriers are willing to have their trailers tracked to give customers greater peace of mind. Montway Auto Transport has the best reputation for finding GPS-friendly carriers.
Insider tips for booking a quality carrier at a good price
"Ask the broker if they have a 'preferred carrier' list of companies that they have vetted for reliability and, depending on the circumstances, request an assignment from that list. After the booking, contact the carrier directly to confirm the details of the transport and ensure the timelines will be adhered to.

The best way to get the cheapest shipping charges is to book in advance, ideally two to four weeks out, as last-minute bookings will often have a premium charge. Another tip is to book your car shipping as terminal to terminal rather than door to door, meaning you drop off and pick up at the nearest carrier’s terminal. You can save $75 to $200 by not incurring the last-mile fee."
—Eduard Chitakhyan, founder and CEO of Tempus Logix

Frequently asked questions

Yes, you can ship your car overseas. You'll typically need to provide a photo ID, proof of ownership, and vehicle registration before an auto transport company will send your car to another country.

You don't need to have auto insurance to ship a car. Carriers (drivers) must have liability insurance.

With open car shipping, cars aren't protected from the weather or flying debris. Enclosed car shipping protects the car inside a trailer. Open car shipping tends to be the most affordable option, but enclosed car shipping is the best way to ensure the car isn't dinged by rocks or hail on the road.

Yes, consider Amtrak Auto Train or Union Pacific for transporting your car by train.

How we review the best car shipping companies

When we first started researching car shipping companies, we noticed an alarming trend: every brand seemed to have irate customers warning others to never use them. Type any car shipping company into Google and you'll find people complaining about lapses in communication, no-show carriers, surprise price increases, and scratched vehicles. 

Such widespread dissatisfaction seems to suggest that the problem isn't necessarily with the companies themselves, but with the car shipping industry as a whole. Brokers provide a popular service by streamlining the hiring process and allowing multiple carriers to bid on each job, which helps lower the final price. Some brokers offer additional perks like extra insurance coverage and quick access to a back-up plan when a carrier drops the ball, but the fact remains that they're middlemen and have little control over the carriers' schedules or communication skills.

Still, there are companies that successfully deliver cars and customer satisfaction more often than others. It's our job to figure out how they do it and who has the best track record.

1. Grading car shipping companies

We started by reading hundreds of customer reviews to identify common complaints. We determined people care most about the following four things:

  • Accurate, transparent pricing with no surprise fees upon delivery.
  • A reliable service with on-time pickup and delivery and responsive customer care.
  • Carriers who communicate about schedule changes and take good care of the vehicle.
  • Some kind of protection or guarantee, often in the form of gap coverage or a damage-free guarantee.

We developed a four-part grading system based on these criteria. Companies earn points in each category, and points equal grades on a scale from A+ to D. We'll adjust our grading criteria as we continue to gather more nuanced information and data, but here's what we currently consider:

  • Price transparency: Online quote calculator functionality and privacy, easily accessible fee explanations, guaranteed quotes, price matching, customer satisfaction regarding the final price. 14 points possible.
  • Reliability: Guaranteed pickup and/or delivery, customer satisfaction regarding timeliness, and customer satisfaction regarding broker's ability to quickly solve problems. 11 points possible.
  • Carrier quality: Transparency regarding carrier vetting process, quality of carrier vetting process, and customer satisfaction with carriers. 6 points possible.
  • Insurance coverage: Bare minimum vs. extra liability coverage, optional gap coverage, and extras like claim assistance, damage-free guarantees, and time to inspect for damage. 11 points possible.


2. Mystery shopping and analyzing customer reviews

To grade a company, we collect information by mystery shopping and analyzing customer reviews on third-party websites like the Better Business Bureau and Trustpilot.

Mystery shopping allows us to experience the brand's website, sales process, and customer service from the perspective of the buyer. For example, some brokers have easy-to-use online quote calculators, while others collect your information and provide a quote over the phone.

Customer reviews give us insight into real experiences, but we tread carefully here because reviews can often be faked. We look for trends that have occurred in the last 12 months and consider warnings from the Better Business Bureau. We calculate a weighted star rating based on all the reviews we can find online. This average customer rating is shared under each brand section but is distinct from the Move.org star rating, which is an editorial score we create to help readers understand the relative value and quality of each company.


3. Interviewing industry leaders

We've also conducted online and in-person interviews with company leaders to learn behind-the-scenes information that sets each one apart. We find these interviews especially helpful in understanding the carrier vetting process.

We've published our car shipping leadership interviews below:

  • Asadullah Sameer Ismailzada, AmeriFreight Auto Transport (coming soon)
  • Mark Scholl, Montway Auto Transport
  • Jack Savov, SGT Auto Transport
  • Terry Williams, Auto Shipping Group


4. Gathering sample quotes

To date, we've collected more than 800 quotes from more than 13 car shipping companies to find industry and company averages. The car shipping quotes include prices for a motorcycle, car, SUV, and pick up truck across multiple distances with both open and enclosed transport and running and non-running vehicles with a one-week lead time. We use the same criteria when gathering quotes so that we can easily compare prices across brands.

We've published many of our quotes on this page and in our individual brand reviews so you can get a sense of how much it might cost to ship your car without having to share your private information.

However, we take cost data with a grain of salt when ranking and reviewing companies that don't guarantee their quotes. Our research shows that the final car shipping price can increase by 25% when all is said and done.


5. Repeating the process

Car shipping is a competitive industry, and companies make changes all the time. We repeat our review methodology at least once per year to ensure we publish up-to-date price averages, customer ratings, and proprietary grades.

Final word: AmeriFreight is the best auto transport company

AmeriFreight Auto Transport is our number one auto transport company because it offers a variety of services and price packages, but each of these transport brokers brings something special to the table:

  • Montway Auto Transport's customer service representatives and experienced carrier network go above and beyond to accommodate special requests.
  • SGT Auto Transport provides the most affordable quotes for open carrier shipping.
  • Sherpa Auto Transport's Price Lock Promise and free car washes keep customers happy.
  • uShip puts you in the driver's seat by allowing you to vet carriers who bid on your job.

Always Active

These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms.    You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.

Performance Cookies

These cookies allow us to count visits and traffic sources so we can measure and improve the performance of our site. They help us to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the site.    All information these cookies collect is aggregated and therefore anonymous. If you do not allow these cookies we will not know when you have visited our site, and will not be able to monitor its performance.

Functional Cookies

These cookies enable the website to provide enhanced functionality and personalisation. They may be set by us or by third party providers whose services we have added to our pages.    If you do not allow these cookies then some or all of these services may not function properly.

Targeting Cookies

These cookies may be set through our site by our advertising partners. They may be used by those companies to build a profile of your interests and show you relevant adverts on other sites.    They do not store directly personal information, but are based on uniquely identifying your browser and internet device. If you do not allow these cookies, you will experience less targeted advertising.
